Let <MATH_0001> be a locally Noetherian scheme. Let
<MATH_0002> be a category fibred in groupoids.
Assume that
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> <MATH_0003>
is representable by algebraic spaces,
<STRUCT_0003> <MATH_0004> satisfies axioms [-1], [0], [1], [2], [3], [4], and [5]
(see Section <REF_0001>),
<STRUCT_0004> <MATH_0005> is a G-ring for all finite type points <MATH_0006> of <MATH_0007>.
<STRUCT_0005>
Then <MATH_0008> is an algebraic stack.

We first prove that <MATH_0001>
is representable by algebraic spaces. To do this it suffices to show
that
<MATH_0002>
is representable by an algebraic space for any affine scheme <MATH_0003> locally
of finite presentation over <MATH_0004> and object <MATH_0005> of
<MATH_0006> over <MATH_0007>, see
Criteria for Representability, Lemma
<REF_0001><FOOTNOTEOPEN_0001>The
set theoretic condition in Criteria for Representability, Lemma
<REF_0002>
will hold: the size of the algebraic space <MATH_0008> representing <MATH_0009> is
suitably bounded. Namely, <MATH_0010> will be locally of finite type and <MATH_0011>
will satisfy axiom [-1]. Details omitted.<FOOTNOTECLOSE_0001>.
Observe that <MATH_0012> is fibred in setoids
(Stacks, Lemma <REF_0003>)
and let <MATH_0013>,
<MATH_0014> be the functor of isomorphism
classes. We will apply
Proposition <REF_0004>
to see that <MATH_0015> is an algebraic space.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Note that
<MATH_0016>
(and hence also <MATH_0017>)
is representable by algebraic spaces by condition (1) and
Criteria for Representability, Lemma <REF_0005>.
Observe that <MATH_0018> is a sheaf for the <ACCENT_0001>tale topology by
Stacks, Lemmas <REF_0006> and
<REF_0007>, i.e.,
axiom [0] holds. Also <MATH_0019> is limit preserving by
Lemma <REF_0008>, i.e., we have [1].
Note that <MATH_0020> has (RS), i.e., axiom [2] holds, by
Lemmas <REF_0009> and
<REF_0010>. Axiom [3] for <MATH_0021> follows
from Lemmas <REF_0011> and
<REF_0012>.
Axiom [4] follows from Lemmas <REF_0013> and
<REF_0014>.
Axiom [5] for <MATH_0022> follows directly from openness of versality
for <MATH_0023> which is part of axiom [5] for <MATH_0024>.
Thus all the assumptions of
Proposition <REF_0015>
are satisfied and <MATH_0025> is an algebraic space.

<STRUCT_0003><STRUCT_0004>
At this point it follows from Lemma <REF_0016>
that <MATH_0026> is an algebraic stack.
